cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet is still bringing the LORD's message against Babylon. Now the call goes out: raise a banner in the land and blow the ram's horn among the nations! That ram's horn is the original group chat notification, friend, and EVERY nation just got pinged.

cards.question: The banner is up and the ram's horn is blowing among the nations. What are the nations being prepared for?

cards.text: Kingdoms get summoned by name, Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz, and horses come up like swarming locusts. That's not a cavalry, friend. That's a WEATHER ALERT.

cards.question: Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz aren't the only ones called up against Babylon. Which kings get prepared for battle too, with their governors and officials?
As the nations get ready, the earth quakes and writhes because the LORD's plans against Babylon have been called off.
The LORD's intentions against Babylon stand. What will they make the land of Babylon?

answers.text: A province ruled by the Medes
A city of refuge for nations

cards.text: Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting and just sit in their strongholds, their strength all used up. I know that move, friend. I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS, and my stronghold was a takeout menu.

cards.question: While Babylon's warriors sit in their strongholds, the bars of her ___ are broken.

cards.text: Babylon's homes are on fire, and the couriers come running to the king, one after another after another. Friend, when your phone buzzes eight times in a row, nobody's texting to say things are FINE.

cards.question: Messenger after messenger races to the king of Babylon. What news are they carrying?

answers.text: His city has been captured from end to end
His army has won the battle at the walls
His enemies have turned around and gone home

cards.question: With the fords seized and the marshes set on fire, Babylon's soldiers stay calm.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, paints a picture: the Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. Friend, I've pressed a LOT of dough flat in my day, but this is a whole other level.

cards.question: Babylon is like a threshing floor being trampled. The LORD says in just a little while, her ___ time will come.

cards.text: Now a new voice speaks up. It's Jerusalem, the dweller of Zion, and she's got something to say about Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

cards.question: Jerusalem says Nebuchadnezzar has devoured her, crushed her and set her aside like an empty vessel. What is she describing?

answers.text: What Babylon has done to her
What she has done to Babylon
What the Medes have done to her

cards.question: Jerusalem asks that the violence done to her and to her flesh be upon ___.

cards.text: Jerusalem has said her piece, and now the LORD answers. Friend, the mystery key I shared that junk drawer with asked which door it opened for YEARS, and nobody EVER answered.

cards.question: After Jerusalem speaks, what does the LORD say He will do for her?

answers.text: Plead her case and take vengeance for her
Leave her case for the nations to settle
Tell her to make peace with Babylon

cards.text: He'll dry up Babylon's sea and her springs, and Babylon will become a heap of rubble, without inhabitant. Well, no PEOPLE anyway, because somebody's moving in.

cards.question: Babylon will become a heap of rubble and a haunt for ___.

cards.text: They'll roar together like young lions and growl like lion cubs. And while they're flushed with heat, the LORD says He'll serve them a feast.

cards.question: The LORD serves them a feast and makes them drunk so they revel. What comes after the party?

answers.text: They fall asleep and never wake up
They wake up and turn back to God
They march out to fight the Medes

cards.text: He'll bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats. Then a cry goes up: "How Sheshach has been captured!"

cards.question: Babylon, once the praise of all the earth, becomes a horror among the nations.

cards.text: Then the sea comes up over Babylon, and she's covered in turbulent waves. Babylon's not on the water anymore, friend. She's UNDER it.

cards.question: After the waves, the picture changes again. What do Babylon's cities become?

answers.text: A dry land where no one lives
A busy land full of traders
A green land full of fields

cards.text: Last, the LORD says He'll punish Bel in Babylon and make him spew out what he swallowed. Bel's been holding on to a lot, friend. Time to give it ALL back.

cards.question: Once Bel is punished, what does the LORD say about the nations streaming to him?

answers.text: They stream to him even more
They build him a bigger temple

cards.question: Even after all this, the wall of Babylon will still be standing.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Trust me, friend, the LORD's message against Babylon isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The opening card already calls this 'the LORD's message against Babylon' just before card 2 asks what the nations are being prepared for. That rules out 'To defend Babylon' and 'To rebuild Babylon', so card 2 has no real choice. The opening card can set the scene without saying which side the nations are called to.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'nobody's texting to say things are FINE' tells the baker the news is bad. That rules out both good-news wrong answers on card 10 ('His army has won the battle at the walls' and 'His enemies have turned around and gone home') before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question itself says Nebuchadnezzar devoured and crushed her. That rules out 'What she has done to Babylon' and 'What the Medes have done to her', so the answer is given in the question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the rest of Jeremiah 51:34: Nebuchadnezzar 'swallowed me like a monster' and 'vomited me out.' This image sets up 51:44, where the LORD makes Bel 'spew out what he swallowed.' Without it, card 14's line has nothing to land on, and the baker misses the link between the two verses.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The key joke doesn't match the action. Jerusalem cries out for justice against Babylon. The key 'asked which door it opened' and nobody answered. That is a different action, so the joke reads as 'huh?'. It also adds a new drawer detail: the backstory gives the key 'endless guesses about its door', not questions that went unanswered.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The blank asks which animal haunts the rubble (jackals, eagles or foxes). Nothing earlier helps the baker reason it out. They can only guess the wording of the line, like the Psalm 23 'anoint with oil' example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'foxes' is a near-match for 'jackals'. Both are wild dogs that roam ruins, and Lamentations 5:18 has foxes prowling desolate Zion. A baker could argue foxes is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'Then a cry goes up' brings in an unnamed crowd or crier. The text doesn't name a new speaker for 51:41. It comes right after the LORD's 'I will' lines and doesn't say anyone else cries out. The card should present the line without inventing a speaker.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Bel shows up for the first time with no word on who he is. The card should say simply who he is, for example Bel, a god of Babylon.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question asks what happens to the nations streaming to Bel. 'They build him a bigger temple' doesn't answer that, while the other two answers are about streaming. It isn't the same kind of answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.
